subject: Clarify slab16k metering, KV credits, and pilot concession for Lumen Retail
messages:
From: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@lumenretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Angela Wong <angela.wong@procureco.com>
Date: 2028-07-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Long-session billing: examples for our recommender agent

Mina / Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo earlier. A quick follow-up from procurement: our recommender uses full session context for niche customers and frequently holds >100k token histories (rolling). Before we scope a pilot, procurement needs a clear write-up of how those sessions will be billed. Specifically:

- How do you bucket/context-slab long sequences? (round up rules, slab sizes)
- Do you apply any credits for KV-cache reuse when identical prefixes are reused across requests?
- How are streaming chunks counted vs final aggregated context?
- Can you provide a sample invoice illustrating rounding on partial slabs?

I attached a couple of session exports so you can see typical token distributions. Procurement would like the rules in writing to present to their finance team. Also flagging Angela in case ProcureCo needs the legal point-of-contact.

Thanks —
Charlie
Charlie Nguyen
Director, AI Product
Lumen Retail
Attachment: session_samples.jsonl (jsonl)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@lumenretail.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-27T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Long-session billing: examples for our recommender agent

Charlie — thanks for the context and the sample exports. I pulled this into our billing team and sketched a proposal below so procurement has something concrete to review. High-level summary first, details after.

Proposal (pilot-friendly):
- Metering unit: "slab16k" = 16,384 token band. Sessions are slabized into contiguous slab16k bands and billed by rounding up to the nearest slab16k for each distinct request in the billing window.
- Residual aggregation: Partial slabs are tracked as residual tokens and aggregated daily; if residuals across an account sum to a full slab16k in the day, that residual converts to a billable slab (reduces overbilling for highly fragmented traffic).
- KV-cache reuse credit: when a request reuses an exact prefix present in an in-memory KV cache (same session id, same model), we apply a 40% token credit to the reused range for invoices (i.e., billed_tokens = billed_tokens - 0.4 * reused_tokens). Credits are calculated per-session and expire after 24 hours.
- Streaming count: streaming chunks are tokenized and counted at emission time, but for long-running streams we attempt prefix collapse at end-of-call; billing will prefer the lower of (sum of emitted tokens) vs (final reconstructed session token count) to avoid double-charge where we can reconcile.

Pilot concession we can offer for Lumen:
- 6-week pilot: waive the first-month slab16k minimums up to 10,000 slab16k-equivalent tokens (one-time credit applied on first invoice).
- 20% discount on the long-context slab16k SKU for pilot months (applied to billable slab16k units after residual aggregation and KV credits).

Next steps: if this aligns, I can send a short term sheet and a sample invoice example. Also need your expected average session length and concurrent sessions to size the pilot.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
Direct: +1 415-555-0182
Attachment: pilot-term-sheet.pdf (pdf)

From: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@lumenretail.com>

Cc: Angela Wong <angela.wong@procureco.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-27T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Long-session billing: examples for our recommender agent

Mina — this looks promising. Procurement will want the following clarified in the term sheet or SOW before we sign:

1) Explicit math example for rounding: show a session with 3 partial slabs (e.g., 10k + 9k + 27k tokens) and how daily aggregation and rounding resolve on invoice.
2) KV-credit mechanics: is the 40% applied before or after rounding? How is 'exact prefix' determined (byte-for-byte? token sequence?).
3) Pilot credit visibility: can you show the credit line item and how it offsets slab billing in month 1?

We expect average session length ~85k tokens, with spikes to 150k in heavy personalization flows; concurrency 120–180. We're happy to proceed with the 6-week pilot & 20% discount but need the invoice example and the exact clause language for rounding/credits.

Angela — can you give a quick heads-up to Procurement that we have a concession proposal on the table?

Thanks,
Charlie

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: finance/legal check on slab16k rules and pilot credit

Mina / Tessa / Sergio — following Charlie's ask, I pulled in a quick note from finance/legal. Key confirmations and suggested wording below so Mina can include in term sheet: 

- Rounding math: billing rounds per request to the next whole slab16k, then daily account-level residuals are summed and converted to billable slabs whenever the day's residual aggregate >= 16,384 tokens. Example line item will show both per-request rounding and the residual conversion.
- KV-credit ordering: credits apply after per-request slab rounding but before residual aggregation conversion. In practice: 1) tokenize and slabize -> 2) round up to per-request slab16k -> 3) subtract KV credits (40% of matched tokens) -> 4) sum residuals for the day and convert any full-slab residuals to billable slabs. This yields deterministic invoices and avoids crediting already-rounded units multiple times.
- Exact prefix: "exact prefix" = token-sequence equality (not byte equality); the system uses canonical tokenization for comparison. For legal purposes we can define this as 'identical tokenized prefix for the same model and session id'.
- Pilot credit line item: finance will accept a one-time invoice credit titled "Pilot slab16k credit — Lumen Retail" and will reduce the amount due for the first invoice; it will be visible on the invoice and in the portal.

I've attached an internal note that sketches the sample invoice flow; finance asks that Mina include a sample spreadsheet so they can validate the credit line and discount application.

Attachment: finance_note.md (md)

V.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Nguyen <charlie@lumenretail.com>, Angela Wong <angela.wong@procureco.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-29T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Long-session billing: examples for our recommender agent

Charlie / Angela — thanks, all. Per finance/legal review above, attached is a sample invoice that walks through three examples (per-request rounding, daily residual conversion, and KV-credit application). Highlights and the final agreed pilot terms below so you have one canonical summary to share with Procurement/Legal: 

Agreed meter & math (final):
- Metering unit: slab16k = 16,384 tokens. Each request is slabized and rounded up to the nearest slab16k.
- KV-cache reuse credit: 40% token credit on tokenized identical-prefix matches; credit applied after per-request rounding and before residual aggregation. Token equality uses Redwood canonical tokenization for the target model. Credits expire after 24 hours.
- Residual handling: partial-slab residuals are summed at the account level daily; when the day's residuals reach >=16,384 tokens they convert to a billable slab16k.

Pilot concession (Lumen Retail):
- 6-week pilot start date on SOW signature.
- One-time "Pilot slab16k credit — Lumen Retail": up to 10,000 slab16k-equivalent tokens applied to first invoice as a credit.
- 20% discount on slab16k SKU applied for pilot months after credits and residual aggregation.

Next: I've attached sample_invoice_rounding_example.xlsx which includes the arithmetic on Charlie's example (10k + 9k + 27k in a single session) and shows how the KV credit and daily residual logic change the billed slabs. If that looks good I'll circulate a 1-page SOW and get legal to append the rounding & KV-credit clause.

Please confirm and we will prepare the SOW.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sample_invoice_rounding_example.xlsx (xlsx)
